checkpoints.name: two_domains_and_a_synchronizer
checkpoints.description: NetCrux: the SoC is a producer (clk_a domain), a consumer (clk_b domain) and a two-flop synchronizer between them. Identifying the clock domains and what does — and does not — cross safely is the heart of the project.

checkpoints.name: synchronizer_is_two_flops
checkpoints.description: NetCrux: the synchronizer is exactly two flip-flops in series — the correct structure for a single-bit crossing. The data bus, by contrast, crosses with no synchronizer at all.

checkpoints.name: safe_path_regression_green
checkpoints.description: SimCrux: the safe request path works — the synchronized request is a clean two-flop value and drives a capture. The regression does NOT assert the captured data, because that path is the hazard.

checkpoints.name: reset_state
checkpoints.description: WaveCrux: during reset the captured register is zero.

cross_tool_deep_links.name: unsynced_data_across_tools
cross_tool_deep_links.source_action: having found in the structure that the 8-bit data bus crosses clk_a to clk_b with no synchronizer, examine that bus in the waveform
cross_tool_deep_links.expected_target_state: the data bus and the clk_b capture edge are shown; because data changes every clk_a with no synchronizer, a clk_b sample can land mid-transition — the multi-bit CDC hazard the structure predicted
